Battles|Armed clash.description: Two or more armed groups engaged in direct combat, exchanging fire or fighting each other in a defined location or area.

Battles|Government regains territory.description: State military or security forces successfully recaptured and reasserted control over an area previously held by an opposing armed group.

Battles|Non-state actor overtakes territ.description: An armed non-state group — such as a militia, rebel faction, or insurgency — seized control of a location or territory previously held by another party.

Protests|Peaceful protest.description: Civilians gathered publicly to express political, social, or economic grievances through non-violent means such as marches, demonstrations, sit-ins, or rallies.

Protests|Protest with intervention.description: A protest was met with intervention by security forces or authorities, such as dispersal attempts, arrests, or the use of crowd-control measures.

Protests|Excessive force against protest.description: Security or state forces responded to protesters with disproportionate or lethal force, resulting in injuries, deaths, or widespread harm to demonstrators.

Explosions/Remote violence|Air/drone str.description: A location was struck by munitions delivered from the air, whether by manned aircraft such as jets or helicopters, or by unmanned aerial vehicles (drones).

Explosions/Remote violence|Shelling/arti.description: Heavy, indirect-fire weapons such as artillery, mortars, rocket launchers, or ballistic missiles were used to strike a target from a distance.

Explosions/Remote violence|Suicide bomb.description: An attacker deliberately detonated explosives strapped to or carried on their body, sacrificing their own life in order to inflict maximum casualties on a target.

Explosions/Remote violence|Remote explos.description: A concealed or planted explosive device — such as a landmine, booby trap, or improvised explosive device (IED) — detonated either remotely or upon contact.

Explosions/Remote violence|Grenade.description: A handheld explosive device was thrown or launched at a target, causing a localized but potentially deadly blast in the immediate vicinity.

Explosions/Remote violence|Chemical weap.description: Toxic or harmful chemical agents were deployed as weapons against people, causing injury, illness, or death through exposure to poisonous substances.

Violence against civilians|Attack.description: Armed actors directly targeted non-combatant civilians with violence — including shootings, stabbings, beatings, or other physical assaults intended to harm or kill.

Violence against civilians|Abduction/for.description: Civilians were unlawfully seized, kidnapped, or made to disappear — often by armed groups or state actors — without legal process, transparency, or acknowledgment.

Riots|Mob violence.description: A crowd or mob engaged in collective violence, attacking people, properties, or communities — often spontaneously and with significant destruction or casualties.

Riots|Violent demonstration.description: A protest or public demonstration escalated into violence, with participants engaging in physical confrontations, property damage, or clashes with security forces.

Strategic developments|Arrests.description: One or more individuals were detained, arrested, or taken into custody by authorities or armed actors, often in connection with conflict-related or politically motivated activity.

Strategic developments|Looting/property.description: Property was deliberately damaged, burned, or destroyed, or goods and assets were looted from homes, businesses, or public infrastructure during conflict or unrest.

Strategic developments|Agreement.description: Two or more parties reached, signed, or publicly announced a formal agreement — such as a ceasefire, peace deal, political accord, or negotiated arrangement.

Strategic developments|Headquarters or b.description: An armed group, military force, or political actor set up a new operational headquarters, base of operations, or command post in a specific location.

Strategic developments|Change to group/a.description: A significant internal or operational change occurred within an armed group or movement, such as a leadership transition, merger, split, rebranding, or shift in tactics.

Strategic developments|Disrupted weapons.description: An attempt to use, transport, or deploy weapons was intercepted, blocked, or prevented — including seizures of arms caches, dismantled bomb plots, or neutralized threats.

Strategic developments|Non-violent trans.description: Control or administration of a geographic area changed hands between parties through negotiation, withdrawal, or agreement rather than through armed combat or coercion.

Strategic developments|Other.description: A strategically significant development was recorded that does not fit neatly into any other defined subtype, but nonetheless represents a meaningful shift in the conflict landscape.

default.description: A conflict or security event was recorded at this location, but its event type and sub-event category have not yet been mapped to a specific classification in this system.
